chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who made it upon himself to walk to the House of Allah, but could not do it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him perform Hajj riding.'

key_terms.الْمَشْيَ: Walking (as a form of worship or vow fulfillment)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone vows to walk to the Kaaba but cannot?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the vow to walk to the Kaaba is not an absolute constraint but a means to intensify devotion; thus, if physical inability arises, the obligation is satisfied by performing Hajj while riding. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-yamin* (vows), where the spirit of the vow is preserved through the act of worship itself, even if the specific mode changes due to necessity. It highlights the balance between strict adherence to vows and the facilitation (*taysir*) granted by the Imams to prevent undue hardship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who made it upon himself for the walking to the House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, but could not do it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him go to Hajj, riding’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who makes a vow and commitment to walk to the House of Allah but cannot do so. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must perform al-Hajj riding.’”
